name: Plant-based meat alternatives (burgers, sausages, nuggets; pea/soy/wheat-protein base)
anchor: per-commodity sovereign metallic-contamination schedules for terrestrial animal foods — Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (the only credible instrument on the register with a complete meat, poultry and egg panel), EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 for cadmium in muscle meat, and FSANZ Schedule 19 for lead in muscle meat; canned forms additionally carry the canned-foods tin maximum level, and the plant-protein analogue row reads across from EU and Hong Kong pulse, soy and cereal commodity maximum levels
native_basis_label: as sold, finished formulated product (wet weight for chilled and frozen forms, product as placed on market for dry mixes); dry-commodity component maximum levels are applied to the hydrated finished product with no dry-to-wet conversion, which is the looser of the two available treatments and is disclosed as such, so certification additionally requires documented source-commodity compliance for every protein ingredient
scope_note: Formulated meat analogues whose protein is wholly plant-derived: pea- and other pulse-protein isolates and concentrates, soy protein isolate, concentrate and textured soy protein, and wheat gluten/seitan, sold as burgers, patties, sausages, nuggets, grounds, strips and deli-style slices. Fungal-biomass (mycoprotein) and precision-fermentation products route to Category 29; dairy- and egg-based analogues route to their own categories; a blended meat-and-plant product is certified on the processed-meats row against the stricter of the two rows' applicable values, cell by cell. Any formulation incorporating rice or rice protein additionally carries the sovereign rice inorganic-arsenic maximum level, which is named as the companion instrument in the iAs cell.
basis_guard: (wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed|as sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part|fresh weight)
basis_guard_note: Category 11 is a dietary as-sold wet-weight category. The guard admits only register rows whose basis is a food-matrix content basis (wet weight, portion ordinarily consumed, product as placed on market, commodity, edible part, food as listed in the Cap 132V schedule). It rejects, by construction, food-contact specific-migration limits, toy and article element-migration limits, animal-feed 12%-moisture bases, dry-matter fertiliser limits, colour-additive ingredient purity specifications, and drinking-water statutory limits. A migration or purity-specification number is not a maximum level for a food and must never anchor a meat, poultry, or egg row.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only initial setting: the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact product form in its native basis; disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; control where neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.label: strictest applicable principal-component lead maximum level; the pulse and legume-vegetable rows bind at 100 ug/kg over the looser cereal row at 200 ug/kg
Pb.substantiation: No credible sovereign government sets a lead maximum level for a meat analogue, so the exact cell is unregulated and the ceiling reads across from the maximum levels governing the principal protein components. Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 0.1 mg/kg for pulses and 0.1 mg/kg for legume vegetables, the commodity classes from which pea and soy protein are drawn; FSANZ Schedule 19 sets 0.2 mg/kg for cereals, the class from which wheat gluten is drawn. The strictest applicable component value binds at 100 ug/kg, so a wheat-gluten-based analogue is held to the pulse ceiling rather than the looser cereal one. BASIS TREATMENT, DISCLOSED IN THE DIRECTION IT ACTUALLY CUTS: the component maximum levels are written on dry commodities as placed on the market and are applied to the hydrated finished product as sold, with no dry-to-wet conversion, because Method v2.0 forbids inventing a basis conversion. That is the LOOSER of the two available treatments, not a conservative one: a hydrated extrudate is mostly water, so a protein ingredient can exceed its own commodity maximum level and still leave the finished product inside this ceiling. The programme states that openly and closes the gap with a second, independent requirement rather than with a conversion factor: every certified lot must carry supplier documentation of the source commodity for each protein ingredient, tested against the named component maximum levels in the commodity own basis, in addition to finished-product compliance against this ceiling. The ingredient-basis treatment is the natural candidate for the first Standards Ratchet review on this row once eligible certified-lot data exist.

Cd.label: strictest applicable principal-component cadmium maximum level; the EU pulses row binds at 40 ug/kg over soy beans at 200 and wheat gluten at 150
Cd.substantiation: EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I sets cadmium maximum levels for each of this row's principal protein commodities: pulses 0.040 mg/kg, soy beans (with peanuts) 0.20 mg/kg, and wheat gluten (with rice, quinoa and wheat bran) 0.15 mg/kg. The strictest applicable component value binds at 40 ug/kg. This is the tightest cell in Category 11 and it is deliberately not relaxed toward the soy row: the method takes the strictest applicable component maximum level, and a soy-based analogue is not entitled to the looser oilseed ceiling merely because soy is the protein it happens to use.

tAs.label: strictest applicable principal-component total-arsenic maximum level; Hong Kong Cap. 132V cereals other than rice binds at 500 ug/kg over the FSANZ cereal-grain row at 1000
tAs.substantiation: No credible sovereign government sets a total-arsenic maximum level for pulses, peas, soy beans or a meat analogue. The nearest applicable component cells are the cereal rows that govern the wheat-gluten component: Hong Kong Cap. 132V cereals other than rice at 0.5 mg/kg and FSANZ Schedule 19 cereal grains and milled cereal products at 1.0 mg/kg. Both are named and the stricter binds at 500 ug/kg. Rice is deliberately excluded from the component set and from the audit scope: a rice-containing formulation is governed by the far more consequential sovereign rice INORGANIC-arsenic maximum levels, which are handled as the companion instrument in the iAs cell rather than folded into a total-arsenic average here.

iAs.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for pulses, peas, soy beans, wheat gluten or a plant-protein meat analogue. Every credible inorganic-arsenic instrument on the register is scoped to rice and rice products, fruit and vegetable juices, infant foods, or seafood. A not-material determination is REJECTED because a real and formulation-dependent inorganic-arsenic pathway exists in this row: rice protein and rice flour are common binders and protein extenders in meat analogues, and rice is the single most arsenic-accumulating food crop. The cell is therefore a control with a formulation-triggered reflex, and no ceiling is invented for the non-rice formulation.
iAs.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS speciation. Speciation is MANDATORY on every lot whose declared formulation contains rice, rice protein, rice flour, rice starch or rice syrup, and reflex-triggered on any other formulation whose total-arsenic screen is quantifiable above the method limit of quantitation. A rice-containing lot is additionally assessed against the sovereign rice inorganic-arsenic maximum level named as this cell's companion instrument, and the stricter applicable value binds.

tHg.label: read-across from the Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-mercury maximum level covering wheat and wheat flour (20 ug/kg), the only credible sovereign mercury value governing any principal component of this row
tHg.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 0.02 mg/kg total mercury for rice, husked rice, polished rice, maize, maize flour, wheat and wheat flour. That row governs the cereal component from which wheat gluten is drawn and is the only credible sovereign mercury maximum level applicable to any principal component of a plant-protein analogue; no credible instrument sets a mercury value for pulses or soy beans. It binds at 20 ug/kg, which is stricter than the 50 ug/kg terrestrial-meat mercury ceiling elsewhere in this category. That asymmetry is a fact about the sovereign instruments and is disclosed, not harmonised: the method selects the strictest applicable component value and does not adjust a plant-matrix ceiling upward to match an animal-matrix one. The EU cereal mercury figure of 0.01 mg/kg was reviewed and NOT used because it is a pesticide maximum residue level, a different regulatory instrument in a different basis, and pesticide-residue instruments are excluded from contaminant anchoring.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. A plant-protein meat analogue carries no methylation pathway and no aquatic trophic transfer, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), so it is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury cell (20 ug/kg total mercury, Hong Kong Cap. 132V wheat row). No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling and none is set by any credible sovereign government for this product form.
MeHg.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell; methylmercury speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total-mercury result approaches the binding total-mercury maximum level, or where the formulation incorporates a fish, fish-meal, or marine-derived ingredient, which would additionally route the lot to the Category 6 seafood mercury ceilings.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury content limit for meat, poultry, game, eggs, or meat analogues. The credible methylmercury instruments (EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, FSANZ Schedule 19, Hong Kong Cap. 132V) are scoped exclusively to fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic animals. Methylmercury is a species of, and arithmetically bounded by, total mercury.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I); UK retained contaminants law; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (CPG 540.600); FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations Part 2 Schedule — none sets a methylmercury limit for a terrestrial animal food, an egg, or a plant-protein meat analogue.

Ni.label: strictest applicable principal-component nickel maximum level; the EU cereals row binds at 800 ug/kg over legume vegetables 1000, pulses 4000 and soy beans 6000
Ni.substantiation: This is the one row in Category 11 where nickel is NOT a control, because the EU nickel maximum levels are drawn over exactly the plant commodities this row is formulated from. All four applicable component rows are named and disclosed: cereals 0.8 mg/kg, legume vegetables 1.0 mg/kg, pulses 4.0 mg/kg, soy beans and edamame 6.0 mg/kg. The strictest applicable component value binds at 800 ug/kg. Nickel matters here in a way it does not for muscle meat: pulses and soy are genuine nickel accumulators, and catalytic hydrogenation of plant fats is a nickel pathway, so a plant-protein analogue is the form in which a nickel ceiling is both available and warranted. The looser soy-bean oilseed row (15 mg/kg) and dry-bean row (12 mg/kg) were reviewed and not adopted: they describe whole oilseed and dry pulse commodities rather than the protein fraction used here, and adopting them would loosen the ceiling by an order of magnitude for no instrument-compelled reason.

Sn.rationale: Inorganic tin in food is a tinplate-packaging pathway: tin migrates into the food from the internal surface of an unlacquered or damaged tinplate can, which is why every credible sovereign tin maximum level on the register is written against canned food rather than against the food itself. A chilled, frozen or film-packed plant-protein meat analogue is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that the canned-food maximum levels exist to control is absent and no sovereign number governs the cell. A lot of this product form that is retorted or packed in a metal can is not certified against this row at all: it is certified against the canned-meats row, whose tin cell carries the binding canned-foods maximum level. No tin ceiling is invented for the non-canned form.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Any quantifiable tin in a lot declared as non-metal-packed triggers a packaging and contact-surface investigation (can or closure liner, tinned equipment, solder) before release, and re-routes the lot to the canned-meats row if metal packaging is found.

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium maximum level for pulses, soy, wheat gluten or a plant-protein meat analogue. The credible aluminium values on the register are drinking- and bottled-water statutory limits, a food-contact specific-migration limit, toy element-migration limits, and the FSANZ infant-formula maximum levels; none can anchor this row, and an adult food must not borrow an infant-formula value. No read-across is supportable and no ceiling is invented. Aluminium nonetheless warrants a named control on this row specifically, because aluminium-containing acidity regulators, firming agents and anti-caking agents are permitted in formulated plant products and because protein isolation uses aluminium-bearing processing equipment.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU and per protein-isolate supplier. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to declared aluminium-containing additives and processing aids, to the isolate supplier's extraction chemistry, and to aluminium contact surfaces and packaging. No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium in food is dominated by benign trivalent chromium, an essential trace element; the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, which does not persist in this matrix (see the Cr-VI cell). The Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level is a real sovereign limit and is published here, but it is recorded as a SCREEN: it is a contact-surface and equipment-leaching tripwire, not a standalone protective ceiling, and it is excluded from the firm-limit count.
Cr.label: read-across from the Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level for pulses (1000 ug/kg), published as a screen; the cereals entry in the same instrument carries the identical value
Cr.substantiation: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium maximum level for a meat analogue. Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 1 mg/kg for pulses and 1 mg/kg for cereals, the two principal component commodity classes; the pulses row is named and the cereals row is disclosed at the same value, so the binding number is unaffected by which component dominates the formulation. Published as a screen because total chromium is dominated by trivalent chromium and is not the health-relevant analyte; the screen functions here as an extruder and stainless-contact tripwire, high-moisture extrusion being the defining unit operation of this product form. Hong Kong's stricter row for vegetables other than pulses (0.5 mg/kg) was reviewed and not adopted: minor vegetable, starch and hydrocolloid ingredients are not principal protein components of this row, and a lot whose formulation is principally vegetable rather than pulse, soy or cereal protein is routed to the vegetable rows in Categories 27 and 28 instead.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in this matrix. A hydrated, cooked, high-protein extrudate is a reducing medium; Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by plant-matrix reductants (ascorbate, phenolics, thiols) and by the heat and shear of high-moisture extrusion, so a Cr(VI) figure reported on such a matrix is an artifact of the extraction chemistry of the total-chromium screen rather than a measurement of a species that persists in the food. The determination follows the reference-method adjudication recorded for the hexavalent-chromium cell in the infant-formula category, applied here to a plant-protein extrudate. Hexavalent chromium is in any event a species of, and bounded by, the published total-chromium screen (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
Cr-VI.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-chromium screen (Cr cell). Alkaline-extraction Cr(VI) determination (IC-ICP-MS) is reflex-triggered only where the total-chromium screen exceeds the published screen value, in which case the investigation is directed at the extruder barrel, screws and die and at stainless slurry-handling surfaces.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food. Every credible Cr(VI) instrument on the register is an article, textile, leather, toy-migration, tattoo-ink, fertiliser or electrical-equipment limit in a non-food basis, and applying one to a food matrix would be a basis conflation the compiler's basis guard rejects.
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915; Regulation (EU) 10/2011; Directive 2009/48/EC; REACH restrictions); UK; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA; FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule — none sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for food.
